provenance.title: God Object
provenance.metric: patterns[name === "God Object"].files — analyzed files where isCode !== false && functions.length > 15 (index.html detectPatterns `godFiles`); the same predicate behind the `N Large Files` architecture issue. `functions` is the headless parser count over raw text and `isCode` gates files absent from codeExts (notably `.mts`).
provenance.baseCountNote: the issue was filed with 63 files at analyzedAt 1791738325602 against the then-main. The immutable base below (origin/main after #2001/#2003) reports 38 God Object files: the earlier refactors already split part of the filed set. Acceptance is the drop on the delivered branch, not the filed number.
provenance.afterTipNote: the after snapshot is the code tree (the split commits) measured with the pinned analyzer; the record, its oracle and the fixture are `.mts`, `.json` and `.md`, none of which the analyzer scores as code, so the God Object count is identical.

tradeoffs.godObject: 38 -> 22 flagged files (-16, -42.1 %); every touched original and sibling lands <= 15, so each of the 16 split families leaves the flagged set. No new sibling is itself flagged, so the drop is exactly the number of split families.
tradeoffs.coupling: 116 -> 120 flagged files. Splitting a `package main` test file mints a new file that references the same package-level helpers/constants as its siblings, so the #2002 coupling heuristic (a file that references more than 8 defining files) counts each new sibling as coupled. The production import graph is unchanged and `functions` is identical (3539 both sides).
tradeoffs.complexity: 178 -> 183 flagged files. The split moves whole declarations verbatim, but the newly minted sibling files carry the same raw-text branch tokens (comments and string literals included) as the originals, and the `1 + Σ(hits) > 30` ceiling is token-proportional, so a handful of new siblings edge over it. The issue under test is God Object, so the drop is delivered and the cost is recorded here rather than hidden.
tradeoffs.functions: unchanged (3539 both sides) — no function was added, removed or renamed; every split moves whole top-level declarations between files.
tradeoffs.approach: test-file splits and cohesive module splits: whole declarations move verbatim (Go between files of `package main`, Python between modules of one package) so the compiler/tests are the verification. The Python safety-net suite is deferred with a reason below.

deferred.reason: no Rust toolchain in the pipeline image — splits under embedded/docker/ui cannot be compiled or tested in-gate (#2002/#2003 precedent)
the embedded .sh/.js/.mjs splits need the Dockerfile COPY set and the codeflow bridge/shim copy-set updated in the same change; deferred to the change that owns those boundary guards

the offline safety-net suite (106 functions, 62 tests) needs ~8 scenario modules and a harness split. Its two largest TestCase classes carry 21 functions each, so landing every sibling <= 15 requires base-class declarations that add names per split — a structural change to the very suite that guards the package, not the verbatim move this change can verify in-gate. Deferred to its own recorded change (architecture trade-off), while its two smaller siblings (registries.py, transport.py) and the refactor guard are split here.

every remaining TS/Python flag needs a multi-module decomposition, not a single extraction: osv-scanner.ts's severity half carries 72 of its branch hits and last-json-scanner.ts's string-state machine 80, and server.py (386) needs roughly a dozen modules because its inline _BRIDGE_JS/_UI_REWRITES string literals carry 84 of its hits. Shipping the plan's one-file seam would leave both siblings flagged and not move the metric.
